on-selected-text
================

[![Lint](https://github.com/uxiew/on-selected-text/actions/workflows/lint.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/uxiew/on-selected-text/actions/workflows/lint.yaml) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/on-selected-text.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/on-selected-text)

A tiny Rust library for retrieving the currently selected text across macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Corresponding Node.js package: [node-on-selected-text](https://github.com/uxiew/on-selected-text/tree/main/bindings/node)

## Install

```bash
cargo add on-selected-text
```

## Quick usage

```rust
use on_selected_text::get_selected_text;

fn main() {
    match get_selected_text() {
        Ok(selected_text) => println!("selected text: {}", selected_text),
        Err(error) => eprintln!("error occurred while getting selected text: {error}"),
    }
}
```

`get_selected_text()` keeps the legacy behavior: when no text is selected, it returns an empty string.

## Typed API

Use the options-based API when your application needs precise errors or optional bounds support:

```rust
use on_selected_text::{get_selected_text_with_options, GetTextError, GetTextOptions};

fn main() {
    let opts = GetTextOptions::default().with_bounds();

    match get_selected_text_with_options(opts) {
        Ok(selection) => {
            println!("selected text: {}", selection.text);
            if let Some(bounds) = selection.bounds {
                println!("bounds: {},{} {}x{}", bounds.x, bounds.y, bounds.width, bounds.height);
            }
        },
        Err(GetTextError::NoTextSelected) => println!("no text selected"),
        Err(error) => eprintln!("failed to get selected text: {error}"),
    }
}
```

See [`docs/API.md`](docs/API.md) for API semantics, [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the current module layout and roadmap, [`docs/NODE_DISTRIBUTION.md`](docs/NODE_DISTRIBUTION.md) for Node package planning, and [`docs/RELEASE.md`](docs/RELEASE.md) for Cargo/npm release steps.

## Node.js binding

An experimental `napi-rs` binding lives in [`bindings/node`](bindings/node). It currently exports Pull and Push APIs:

```ts
import { checkPermissions, getSelectedText, startSelectionDaemon } from 'node-on-selected-text'

console.log(checkPermissions())
console.log(await getSelectedText({ fetchBounds: true }))

const daemon = startSelectionDaemon(
  { triggerDelayMs: 120, getTextOptions: { fetchBounds: true } },
  (error, selection) => {
    if (!error) console.log(selection.text, selection.bounds)
  },
)
```

Build it locally from the package directory:

```bash
cd bindings/node
npm install
npm run build
npm test
npm run test:binding
npm run pack:dry-run
npm run verify:platform-packages
npm run smoke
# 交互式真实选区验证：倒计时内切到目标应用并选中文字
npm run smoke:interactive
# 可断言验证：用于真实应用回归和发布前人工门禁
npm run smoke:interactive -- --expect-contains "expected text"
```

`npm run smoke` 会加载 native addon、检查权限并尝试读取当前真实选区。命令行会抢占焦点，因此真实应用验证建议用 `npm run smoke:interactive`，在倒计时期间切回 TextEdit、浏览器或 VS Code 并选中文字；倒计时结束后脚本会等待短暂 settle 并对 `AX focused element` / pasteboard 瞬态失败做有限重试。发布前或复现特定应用时可追加 `--expect-text`、`--expect-contains`、`--expect-regex`、`--min-length`，脚本会输出 `assertion` JSON 并用退出码表示断言结果。macOS 下如果返回 `permission.status = "denied"`，请给运行 Node 的宿主应用开启 Accessibility 后重试；系统权限提示需要应用显式请求，单纯读取失败不会保证自动弹窗。

The npm package is distributed as a tiny root JS loader plus platform-specific optional dependency packages. The root package does not include `.node` binaries; npm resolves only the package matching the current `os` / `cpu` / Linux `libc`.

The `Node Binding` GitHub Actions workflow builds the addon on macOS / Windows / Linux, runs JS and native binding smoke tests, and verifies npm package contents with `npm pack --dry-run`. The `Node Release` workflow builds six platform prebuilds, assembles napi-rs optional dependency packages under `bindings/node/npm`, and only publishes to npm when manually dispatched with `publish=true`.

## Push daemon

`start_selection_daemon()` starts a RAII-managed background worker. macOS uses a listen-only CGEventTap, Windows uses a low-level `WH_MOUSE_LL` hook, Linux uses AT-SPI2 ObjectEvents, and unsupported or unavailable event sources fall back to a portable polling bootstrap. All paths reuse the typed Pull API, deduplicate repeated results, and stop when `DaemonHandle` is dropped.

## Platform notes

### macOS

The library first tries the Accessibility API, uses `AXSelectedTextRange` to distinguish an actual empty selection from an app that needs fallback, and can return `AXBoundsForRange` rectangles when `GetTextOptions::with_bounds()` is enabled. It retries once with `AXManualAccessibility` for Chromium/Electron-style accessibility trees. If fallback is needed, Rust manages an NSPasteboard transaction, snapshots/restores multiple pasteboard items with transient/concealed/autogenerated markers, uses AppleScript only to send `Cmd+C`, and reads the best text representation from plain text, RTF/HTML, file paths, or URLs.

Applications using this crate should call `check_permissions()` at startup and guide users to enable Accessibility permission when needed.

### Linux

The library first tries the focused AT-SPI2 Text selection and can return Text range extents when `GetTextOptions::with_bounds()` is enabled. On Wayland and X11, it then reads the PRIMARY selection, which avoids simulated key presses and normal clipboard pollution. If native primary selection providers are unavailable, it falls back to the guarded clipboard path when enabled.

### Windows

The library first tries the focused UIAutomation TextPattern2/TextPattern selection and can return TextRange bounding rectangles when `GetTextOptions::with_bounds()` is enabled. If UIAutomation is unavailable, it uses a guarded clipboard fallback:

- process-level mutex to avoid concurrent copy/restore races;
- clipboard snapshot and Drop-based restore;
- Windows raw clipboard-format snapshot for fallback restore;
- sentinel polling instead of a fixed sleep;
- Windows clipboard history/cloud-sync blocking markers during fallback.

Push debounce tuning and real-application coverage refinements are planned as incremental follow-up work.

## Release

See [`docs/RELEASE.md`](docs/RELEASE.md). Cargo publishing uses `cargo publish --dry-run --registry crates-io` as the local gate. npm publishing should run through GitHub Actions trusted publishing so the platform packages are built on native runners and consumers only install the matching binding.

## Development

```bash
cargo fmt
cargo test
cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
```

Manual smoke helpers are available for real desktop coverage:

```bash
cargo run --example pull_smoke -- --bounds
cargo run --example daemon_smoke -- --bounds
```

See [`docs/TEST_MATRIX.md`](docs/TEST_MATRIX.md) for the platform/application checklist.
